Yes. At ~CAD $700/month, I’d focus on small/founder-led studios or modular services, rather than traditional full-service agencies. I found several Toronto options that look relevant.

Studios worth putting on your shortlist

Lab Creative Inc — Toronto brand strategy/design studio. Better suited if your priority is brand identity, positioning, and high-quality creative rather than ongoing social posting.

Walden — A downtown creative/marketing studio explicitly positioned around helping small businesses with branding, web, content, visuals and practical marketing.

DMC Creative — Small-business-focused studio covering websites, branding, graphic design and ongoing marketing, so potentially useful if you need a mixture of creative and digital work.

Maduna Marketing — Focuses on social media and campaign execution for small businesses, e-commerce brands and creators. Their positioning is particularly relevant if you want someone to take day-to-day marketing off your plate.

Creatica Studios™ — East York creative/production studio combining branding, photography/video and campaign execution. Worth considering if visual content is a major part of what you need.

Neighbourhood Creative — West-end studio covering creative direction, photography/video, social, paid ads, websites, influencer/PR and experiential work. It may offer more capability than you need at $700/month, but is worth asking about a narrowly scoped engagement.

One particularly relevant pricing benchmark

myBloom publicly lists a CAD $700/month plan, although it's primarily website + local SEO, rather than a creative/social package. Its managed-social plan is listed at $600/month, while its broader package starts at $1,600/month. 
myBloom

That makes the $700 budget realistic for one focused marketing function, but probably tight for a studio doing strategy + photography/video + social management + ads simultaneously.

How I'd structure the $700

For a local business, I'd be inclined to ask studios for something like:

$500–600/month creative/marketing retainer

4–6 quality social pieces

basic content planning/copy

Google Business Profile/social upkeep

one small monthly creative refresh

$100–200/month

reserved for boosting the strongest piece or testing a small paid campaign

Or, if your business already has decent social content, put the entire $700 into local SEO/Google Business Profile + conversion-focused creative rather than paying someone simply to keep Instagram populated.

One useful comparison is Hot Hot Dog Studio: it's explicitly built around small businesses and offers branding, web, social, ads, email and strategy, but its published inquiry form starts its budget bands at under $1,500/month, so I'd treat it as a stretch rather than assume $700 will work. 
hothotdog.studio

If you tell me what kind of local business you run (restaurant, trades, salon, professional service, retail, etc.), I can narrow this to 3–5 Toronto studios whose services actually fit your $700/month budget and compare what you'd likely get from each.
